reason: The gap addresses a specific aspect of maternal health during pregnancy (weight gain) in relation to Sudden Unexpected Infant Death Syndrome (SUID) compared to other causes of infant death, using a well-defined case-case comparison design. The existing literature indicates that maternal obesity is a risk factor for SUID but does not specify the role of weight gain specifically. This gap would refine current understanding by providing more detailed information on how weight gain during pregnancy relates to SUID relative to other causes of infant mortality.
